scope: Official MCP SDK 2.3.1 two-live-stdio-process boundary in the route-free DNS/HTTP fixture; development binary and checksum-verified unsigned experimental Debian 12 amd64 package
reproduce: Set OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_DIR=$PWD/tools/mcp-sdk-probe and run bash tools/netns_adversarial_probe.sh target/debug/outbound-guard-mcp; for installed replay also set OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE to the verified .deb and OUTBOUND_GUARD_TEST_SDK_PACKAGE_SHA256 to its recorded digest.
checks: Two SDK transports simultaneously keep independent server processes alive. Alternating calls allow 60 GETs in each process, followed by one EGRESS_RATE_LIMIT in each. Each audit has 60 approvals and one denial. The fixture requires exactly 120 allowed.test A queries, 120 AAAA queries and 120 /plain HTTP hits, with no DNS/HTTP for either denied marker URL. Installed replay checks package installation, 128 MiB/64 PID quotas, 64-FD server limit, removal, residue and cleanup in the full suite.
limitations: The rate budget and audit are process-local and can be reset by starting a new process. This is a deliberately exposed boundary, not shared enforcement. No native Codex/Claude/Cursor calls, host-wide packet capture, traffic from other tools, arbitrary process count, official candidate, owner acceptance, independent human review, or AI Scraping Defense repository coverage.
